name: Mount Lofty House
positioning: Adults-only country house hotel in the Adelaide Hills, built in 1852 as Arthur Hardy's summer house on the summit of Mount Lofty and rebuilt after the 1983 Ash Wednesday fires
best_for: Couples who want a historic adults-only escape close to Adelaide
Travelers drawn to valley views, gardens, a day spa and house history

facts.text: Mount Lofty House was built in 1852 by statesman Arthur Hardy as his summer house.
The house was built on the summit of Mount Lofty.
The original house was burnt to the ground in the 1983 Ash Wednesday fires.
After being completely rebuilt, it reopened as a luxury boutique hotel on 12 February 1986.
The manor passed through several South Australian families and was a commune in the 1970s.
The hotel is 15 minutes from Adelaide CBD and 25 minutes from Adelaide airport.
The swimming pool overlooks the Piccadilly Valley.
Spa treatments are offered at Gatekeeper's Day Spa.
Guests can play billiards or chess or relax in the house library.
Guests can explore the Mount Lofty Estate gardens or the neighbouring Botanic Gardens.
Hardy's Verandah Restaurant's wine list has more than 1300 Australian and international wines, housed in the historic 1852 wine cellar.
Hardy's Verandah Restaurant was awarded 3 hats by the Australia Good Food Guide in 2024.

highlights.text: The Concierge hosts a nightly champagne and house history tour.
Sequoia Lodge suites are sustainably designed, with tree-top views over the Piccadilly Valley and vineyards.
Sequoia Lodge has its own reception area, lounge, breakfast room and mineral hot springs.
Piccadilly Valley View rooms in the Piccadilly Wing have views across the Piccadilly Valley, a sitting area and outdoor balconies.

considerations.text: Mount Lofty House is a retreat for adults.
WhataHotel notes the secluded hilltop location requires a car for city access.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning.
